title: Charlie Parker in Kansas City and on the Apollo job
summary: He saw Bird sound bad in Kansas City, return from Oklahoma much improved, and praises his mind and ear while not liking his sound. He recalls Bird learning 'Tico Tico' at a fast tempo at the Apollo.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: I was going to ask you because remember that night I met you when you were playing with Brooks? We were talking about Bird. What did you think when you heard
Bird? Or had you heard him when he was first starting out?

The first time when Bird came out, you know, I was in Kansas City when he first came out to play. He sounded so bad that we wouldn't let him play. And he went down to Oklahoma and stayed about six months with Fletcher Smith who really taught him a lot about his playing. And he came back and just washed everybody out.

The only thing about Bird that didn't really knock me out, and I don't want to take anything away from him because I think the man was a genius and he was -- had an extraordinary musical mind. But his sound, you see, it wasn't a standard sound. Although it fit what he did. Because he couldn't play the first chair no place. Well, he didn't read that well in the first place.

But he had a marvelous ear because I remember one time when they did a job at the Apollo and we had -- I forget who we had playing first sax. I was playing tenor and Bird was playing third. And they had a -- what do you call it?

Juggler. And this guy had the music but it was Tico, Tico and he wanted it at a very rapid speed. And it was so fast that the first man couldn't play it. So Bird said, play it over for me a couple times. And the guy played it over to him and then he started playing it. And he played it for the rest of the week. And it got faster and
faster. And the more faster it got, the more improvisations he put on it. And it was just like taking a saxophone lesson listening to him play this. He was marvelous musician.
